events.statement: B/PB and GF representatives met to set design criteria for the adhesive anchors used to attach the hanging ceiling supports to the concrete tunnel roof, including a factor of safety of two and a switch from stainless steel to A36 threaded fastener material.

quotes.quote:
This meeting focused on the use of adhesive anchors which will be used to attach the hanging
ceiling supports to the concrete tunnel roof.

Date: 10/12/1998
Re: Meeting with B/PB on 10/9/98

events.statement: A memorandum recorded the design criteria directed by P. Das for the adhesive anchors, including a factor of safety of two on manufacturer's ultimate capacities and use of A36 material instead of stainless steel for threaded fasteners.

quotes.quote:
1. For the one-hanger out scenario:
a. use a factor of safety of two (2) applied to manufacturer's ultimate capacities to
arrive at allowable capacity for adhesive design.
2. Stainless Steel will no longer be used for threaded fasteners. Use A36 material.

events.statement: NRC 1000 Gold Epoxy was used in the I-90 eastbound connector tunnel from June 1999 through March 2000 without being on the Massachusetts Highway Department's qualified list.

quotes.quote:
Why was the NRC 1000 Gold Epoxy used in the I-90
East-bound connector tunnel from June 1999 through March 2000,
without being on the Massachusetts Highway Department of
State's qualified list?

events.statement: Modern Continental Construction (MCC) sent a letter to Bechtel/Parsons Brinckerhoff (B/PB) regarding adhesive anchor movement, which was later referenced in a November 1999 letter about additional anchor testing.

quotes.quote:
Reference: MCC Letter No. 0114, dated 10/07/99
B/PB Letter No. 0350. dated 10/12/99
MCC Letter No. 0139, dated 11/08/99

events.statement: B/PB directed action items after adhesive anchor movement was found, including having Modern Continental Construction contact the anchor bolt supplier, confirm uniform hanger loading, and having B/PB reconfirm ceiling load calculations.

quotes.quote:
To summarize, the action items from our October 12, 1999 letter:
1. MCC to contact the supplier of the adhesive anchor bolt system, review the installation of the
failed anchors and obtain a manufacturer's recommendation.

4. B/PB will confirm that ceiling load calculations are correct.
Action has been completed, B/PB has re-confirmed that design loads for the ceiling
system are correctly stated.

events.statement: B/PB denied Modern Continental Construction's claim that additional testing of adhesive anchors was a change to the contract, stating the ceiling had not been installed in accordance with the contract because anchors were over-torqued and ceiling hangers were not loaded uniformly.

quotes.quote:
We do not concur with your position that all elements of the ceiling have been installed in accordance
with the Contract. Whereas, adhesive anchors are over torqued and the ceiling hangers are not loaded
uniformly.

Based on the above, the project has determined that there is no merit to MCC's claim for additional
compensation and hereby inform you that this claim is denied.

events.statement: Modern Continental Construction sent a letter later referenced as part of the correspondence leading to Contract Proposal No. 22 for adhesive anchor replacement and re-testing.

quotes.quote: MCC Letter No. C09B2-0165, dated December 29, 1999

events.statement: Modern Continental Construction began retesting ceiling adhesive anchor bolts in the HOV ramp C04A2 area, work that continued into August 2000 and was tracked on time-and-materials slips.

quotes.quote: 03/10/00 - Retesting Anchors in HOV - C04A2 area

MCC has completed re-testing all ceiling adhesive anchors in the C04A2 area. The
anchors were originally tested to 3,250 lbs. tension, per the contract, and then re-tested to 6350
lbs., as directed by the Project.

events.statement: Modern Continental Construction submitted Contract Proposal No. 22 to B/PB seeking $17,102.61 in reimbursement for retesting the ceiling adhesive anchors in the C04A2 area to 6,350 pounds tension.

quotes.quote:
Modern Continental Construction hereby submits a detailed cost
proposal for Contract Proposal (CP) No. 22. The total cost associated with this change, is
Seventeen Thousand One Hundred Two Dollars and Sixty-One Cents ($17,102.61).

events.statement: B/PB issued a fully executed Contract Modification 158FW authorizing $16,396.50 in compensation for re-testing ceiling adhesive anchor bolts in the HOV ramp because several anchors had failed and all installed bolts had to be re-tested at 6,350 pounds tension.

quotes.quote:
Subject: Central Artery (I-93)/Tunnel (I-90) Project
Contract No. 99119-C09B2
I-90 Seaport Access Tunnel Finishes
Contract Modification 158FW - Anchor Bolt Testing In HOV

Due to several failures of ceiling anchor bolts in the HOV, the Project determined that all of the bolts that were installed
had to be re-tested at 6350 lbs. tension.

events.statement: The adhesive anchors along the M1 row of ceiling panel section EB081 pulled out of the tunnel roof, causing the support structure and ten concrete ceiling panels to swing down and to the north in the connector tunnel to the Ted Williams Tunnel.

quotes.quote:
the sequence of fracture and
damage that led to the structure swinging down and to the north after the adhesive anchors
along the “M1” row of ceiling panel section EB081 (module 081 from the eastbound tunnel)
pulled out of the tunnel roof

events.statement: NTSB Materials Laboratory representatives began hand-held borescope inspections of the failure anchor holes in the eastbound tunnel and removed core samples from ten anchor positions in the westbound tunnel ceiling using diamond coring bits.

quotes.quote:
The samples were removed on August 9, 2006
using cylindrical diamond coring bits.

performed hand-held borescope inspections of the
failure anchor holes on August 9 and 10, 2006.

events.statement: James Wildey transported 17 anchors removed from their ceiling fittings in the failure area from the Boston area to the NTSB Materials Laboratory.

quotes.quote:
The 17 anchors from the failure area that had been removed from their fittings were
transported by the undersigned (James Wildey) from the Boston area to the NTSB
Materials Laboratory on August 11, 2006.

events.statement: Core samples containing anchors were transported to the FBI laboratory in Quantico, Virginia, for x-ray inspection to look for voids in the epoxy.

quotes.quote:
the core samples
containing anchors (“WB083-S-8 north”, “WB083-N-3 north”, and “WB083-N-3 south”) were
transported to the laboratory facilities of the Federal Bureau of Investigation, Quantico,
Virginia, on August 22, 2006, where x-ray inspection of the core samples was conducted.

NTSBP060084

events.statement: Laser-scanned images of twenty failure-area anchor holes and selected other holes were acquired by Laser Techniques Company under a contract with the NTSB Materials Laboratory.

quotes.quote:
a contract was developed with Laser
Techniques Company to generate laser-scanned images of the holes. These images were
acquired on September 28 and 29, 2006.

quotes.quote:
DATE IN:
October 18, 2006
P/O #:
NTSB061012

events.statement: The NTSB Materials Laboratory issued Report No. 06-075 documenting the condition of the concrete ceiling panels and support structure after removal from the tunnel and the sequence of fracture that caused the collapse.

quotes.quote:
MATERIALS LABORATORY STUDY REPORT
Report No. 06-075
December 13, 2006

events.statement: The NTSB Materials Laboratory issued Report No. 06-105 identifying the adhesive used in the I-90 tunnel anchorages as a Power-Fast epoxy and describing laboratory testing of Standard Set and Fast Set formulations.

quotes.quote:
December 27, 2006
MATERIALS LABORATORY FACTUAL REPORT
Report No. 06-105

The adhesive that was used in the anchorages in the I-90 tunnel roof had been
preliminarily identified in construction documents as a Power-Fast epoxy

events.statement: The NTSB Materials Laboratory issued Report No. 06-091 detailing examination of the twenty adhesive anchors from the failure area, describing void areas, adhesive failure, and yellowed epoxy found on the failure-area anchors.

February 21, 2007
MATERIALS LABORATORY FACTUAL REPORT
Report No. 06-091

Twenty adhesive anchors from the failure area (ceiling module EB081, middle1 row),
Laser scanned images of the twenty failure anchor holes and selected others
